title: Introduce output gatekeeper for schema handshake and streaming stability in OpenAI compatibility layer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add output gatekeeper to enforce JSON-schema handshake during streaming, map internal schema errors to OpenAI-compatible error codes, and introduce feature-flagged fail-open behavior for staged rollout.
description:
Motivation: Customers use response_format/schema to lock model outputs for downstream tool calls. We observed intermittent streaming truncation and partial object emission when a model and the server disagreed on schema handshake semantics. This PR introduces an 'output gatekeeper' middleware that validates schema conformance during streaming, provides deterministic tool-call fencing, and translates internal error taxonomy into OpenAI-compatible error shapes for the openai-compat adapter.

What this change does: Adds a streaming handshake step at request start that negotiates response_format (v1/v2) and a soft/strict mode. During token streaming the gatekeeper computes a lightweight incremental JSON state, emits checkpoint tokens, and rejects tokens that would irreparably violate the target schema. When violation occurs the gatekeeper can either: (a) fail-closed with a clear GATE-ERR code and resume token for client replay, or (b) fail-open (configuration: gatekeeper.fail_open=true) where the stream continues but a metadata failure event is emitted.

Compatibility: Default rollout is feature-flagged off. The openai adapter maps the following internal codes to OpenAI-style responses: GATE-ERR-SCHEMA => 400 with structured error.payload.schema_error, GATE-ERR-TOOLCALL-FENCE => 409 with tool_call_rejected. When response_format is omitted we preserve previous permissive behavior.

Implementation notes: - New core components: pkg/streaming/gatekeeper.go (handshake + incremental validator), pkg/streaming/checkpoint.go (resume token generation), enterprise/api/compat/openai_adapter.go (error mapping and header injection). - SDK surface: sdk/python/redwood/response_contract.py exposes ResponseContract.validate_stream and ResponseContract.resume_from_token. - Observability: console/telemetry/gatekeeper_metrics.go exposes gatekeeper.schema_violation_count, gatekeeper.resume_token_issued, gatekeeper.fail_open_count. - Config: charts/redwood/templates/gatekeeper-configmap.yaml and console/flags/feature_flags.go add a gatekeeper.enable and gatekeeper.fail_open flags.

Testing & CI: Added integration test tests/integration/test_schema_handshake.py that simulates pausing mid-object and verifies resume token correctness. Unit tests for incremental validation and resume behavior were added. Local stress runs indicate negligible latency overhead (~0.8ms median per-request) when gatekeeper is enabled. CI: all checks passed after a flaky streaming test was stabilized (re-run).

Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (internal canary): gatekeeper.enable = true, gatekeeper.fail_open = true for 10% traffic. - Stage 2: gatekeeper.fail_open = false for 25% traffic, capture telemetry for 7 days. - Stage 3: increase to 100% after monitoring verification.

Docs & examples: Updated docs/api/response_format.md with handshake semantics and examples for resume tokens. Added an example in redwood-quickstarts showing graceful tool-call fencing with strict mode.

Risks & mitigations: Strict fail-closed mode can surface new 400/409 errors for customers with loose models; mitigated by feature flags and a telemetry-backed opt-in. Resume tokens are short-lived (default 5 minutes) and cryptographically signed to avoid replay attacks.

Related: ENG-1247 (schema contract reliability), PM-893 (customer ask: stable tool calls), SUP-4321 (support ticket showing a broken toolcall during streaming).

body_preview: Gatekeeper middleware adds streaming handshake, incremental JSON validation, resume tokens, and OpenAI-compatible error mapping; feature-flagged rollout with telemetry.
